newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish court arrests 21 over Islamist play.
newsitem.headline: Turkish court arrests 21 over Islamist play.

text.p: Turkish security police have arrested 21 people for staging an Islamist play that angered the strictly secularist army, the state-run Anatolian news agency said on Tuesday.

The agency said fifteen were arrested last week and police were questioning them with a view to bringing charges of provoking public hatred and animosity, and weakening and insulting the security forces. Six others, detained on Tuesday, were expected to face similar charges.
It gave no details about the play, called "An enemy of God".
The powerful military has led a chorus of secularist uproar against attempts by Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan to relax strict restrictions on the role of Islam in public life.
Turkish police raided illegal Islamic education centres at the weekend as Erbakan stalled over demands for an anti-Islamist crackdown.
Three directors of illegal Islamic education centres which closed on Monday in western Sakarya province went on trial on Tuesday, the agency reported.
It did not specify the charges against them. Halting illegal Islamic education is one of the generals' main demands.
A preacher close to the Islamist Welfare Party of Erbakan also went on trial on Monday, charged with fostering religious separatism and hatred.
Ali Kucuker, imam of the mosque at the Welfare headquarters in Ankara, faces up to three years in jail if found guilty.

Erbakan signed a National Security Council communique on Saturday agreeing to proceed with curbs on the role of Islam in public life. But senior Welfare Party parliamentarians said they will seek to block any bid by parliament to restrict religious education.
